column1: # JSON SCHEMA EXPORT -- the bridge to every structured-output API.
# The review's finding I / SUPPORT.md act 2. Every major LLM provider's
# structured-output API constrains generation to JSON Schema and to
# nothing else, so without an export a model cannot ride that path and
# then be `vet`ted as the semantic gate -- and an MCP tool's
# `inputSchema`, which the protocol REQUIRES to be JSON Schema, cannot
# be derived from an aontu tool model at all.
# EVERY EXPECTATION HERE WAS OBTAINED BY RUNNING BOTH ENGINES AND
# DIFFING. The expect object is the schema AND the loss report, because
# a schema that silently DROPPED a construct would look identical to one
# that carried it -- and a dropped constraint makes the schema admit
# MORE than the model does, which is the failure this language exists to
# refuse. The CLI's envelope (version, verb) is not compared.
# WHAT CROSSES EXACTLY: kinds to types, concrete scalars to `const`, a
# disjunction of scalars to `enum` (and its preference to `default`),
# bounds to minimum/maximum with the OPEN endpoints as the exclusive
# keywords, `re` to `pattern` (aontu's portable subset is a subset of
# ECMA-262, which is what JSON Schema reads), `neq` to `not: {enum}`
# with `1` and `1.0` carried once, `len` to minLength/maxLength on a
# string, minProperties/maxProperties on a map and minItems/maxItems on
# a list (an open count bound as the next whole number, an excluded
# count as `not` both bounds at it), `unique()` to uniqueItems, optional
# keys to an absence from `required`, `map` and `list` to object and
# array, a disjunction of bare kinds to a `type` array, a bare `*x` to
# x's kind with x as `default`, a written `nil` to the schema `false`
# (it admits nothing), and -- the one aontu and JSON Schema say
# is `additionalProperties: <template>`, which is what it means. A
# written list is `prefixItems` for its positions and `minItems` for
# their count, and it stays OPEN, as the meet does: `[integer, string]`
# admits `[1, "x", true]`, so only `close()` adds `items: false`
# AN EXACT NUMBER CROSSES AS ITS DIGITS: a `0d` literal, `enum` member,
# endpoint or divisor is written as its decimal text, with no loss and
# no rounding through a double, because 2020-12 compares numbers by
# their value (G12 section 4); a consumer that reads the schema with
# binary64 rounds on its own side.
# WHAT DOES NOT, AND IS REPORTED: a `must()`'s message, since the check
# crosses as `allOf` of its trial schema (ADR-055), the exact `0d` kinds,
# which no JSON Schema type holds one leaf of a number for, a kind
# narrowed to one leaf of a number (`integer`, `float`: JSON Schema
# reads a number by its value, and `number & multiple(1)` is the integer
# it means, G12 phase 4), a bound on a
# Schema has no uniqueness-by-property keyword), a hidden entry (not
# generated, so not part of the value a consumer produces), a count with
# no domain, and any residue -- an unresolved reference is not a
# property constraint, and guessing one would be inventing a promise. A
# nil the engine minted and nobody collected is residue; a nil the
# author WROTE is bottom, and crosses.
